algorithm: Build a DAG of operations and closures, topologically sort reachable nodes and propagate adjoints in reverse. Broadcast gradients sum expanded axes. Numerical checks use central differences. Reference: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~./aarti/ML21/lectures/Lecture9.pdf .
architecture: Tensor operations → dynamic DAG → reverse traversal → parameter gradients. Pure expression AST → constant folding → equivalence check. NumPy executes forward array operations.
data_model: Tensor = finite float ndarray, requires_grad, parents, adjoint. Expression nodes are add/mul tuples, numeric constants and named variables.
description: A NumPy reverse-mode autodiff framework with independently checked gradients and a small pure-expression optimizer.
design: Restrict operator semantics and explicitly reject nonfinite tensors. Stable cross entropy subtracts a row maximum treated as a constant; softmax shift invariance makes the derivative correct.
family_notes: Differentiate a quadratic expression and compare central differences.
Reduce broadcast gradients back to the original operand shape.
Check both matrix multiplication paths against finite differences.
Differentiate a linear regression mean-squared error.
Use shifted log-softmax to avoid exponential overflow.
limitations: No GPU backend, custom native matmul or automatic tensor-graph fusion. The expression optimizer is separate from the dynamic Tensor graph. Backward resets all reachable gradients per invocation. Matrix multiplication is 2D only; sum supports one axis. Recursive traversal is unsuitable for extremely deep graphs.
operations: Run finite-difference checks after adding an operator. Test shapes, broadcasting, repeated use and near-boundary domains. Report local timing and numerical error rather than training-scale claims.
scope: Tensor graph with reverse-mode autodiff, scalar/broadcast arithmetic, 2D matrix multiplication, reduction, slicing, stable sigmoid and cross entropy, Linear/MLP modules, SGD and constant/identity folding.
security: Treat this as educational code; review it before handling trusted data.
title: Deep Learning Graph Optimization Framework
